summary.intent: Complete the GSD manager loop for v1.1 milestone gap-closure phases 42 (API unpin integrity), 43 (FUSE write durability), and 44 (IPNS conflict handling) — discuss all three, plan and execute phase 42, then plan and execute 43 and 44.
summary.outcome: Phases 42–44 were fully discussed with CONTEXT.md artifacts committed. Phase 42 was planned (8 plans) and executed (3 waves, all 8 plans complete, 132+ tests green, migrations applied to live DB). Code review was run and committed. Phase 42 close-out (verifier + phase.complete) and phases 43/44 planning+execution remain.

repo: Kubo staging config (docker/docker-compose.staging.yml:62-72) uses the 'server' profile but exposes swarm port 4001 publicly — DHT provider records for every pinned CID are broadcast to the public network despite content being encrypted.
The POST /ipfs/unpin endpoint had no ownership check: any valid JWT holder could unpin any CID. The handler never read req.user.id and passed the CID string directly to Kubo pin/rm.
Writable-share saves drop prunedCids without unpinning (shared-write.ts:450), so there is no legitimate cross-user unpin path — any cross-user unpin is malicious or accidental.
BYO provider.unpin was broken in both directions before phase 42 — the server-side fix handles it for free via the 'not pinned' advisory-only swallow.

pnpm filter + test double-dash bug: `pnpm --filter @cipherbox/api test -- --testPathPattern=X` breaks because pnpm inserts its own `--` separator, making jest treat the pattern flag as a positional regex. Correct form: `pnpm --filter @cipherbox/api exec jest --testPathPattern='X'`
1Password SSH commit signing requires dangerouslyDisableSandbox: true on all git commit calls; agent-level signing errors require the user to restart the 1Password desktop app to recover.

No .prettierignore existed before this session — prettier was mangling .planning/ docs and breaking regex patterns embedded in VALIDATION.md tables (pipe characters interpreted as table column separators).
gsd commit helper 'committed: false' is an unreliable false negative — the commit often lands anyway. Always verify with git log before retrying.

code.finding: Web unpin errors are silently swallowed via .catch(logger.warn) — clients never read the HTTP response from unpin, making the choice between 403 and 2XX a forward-looking API contract decision only.

Kubo v0.40 with 'server' profile. The server profile disables local-network discovery only — it keeps full public DHT participation. Swarm port 4001 tcp+udp is externally exposed, so all pinned CIDs are advertised via provider records.

guardedUnpin added with pg_advisory_xact_lock(hashtext(cid)), transactional row-delete + refcount + pending_unpins outbox insert, Kubo pin/rm post-commit best-effort. Cross-user attempt increments cipherbox_unpin_cross_user_attempts_total and returns silently.

Upload compensation path fires a global pin/rm on a CID that content-addressed dedup may share with another user — this is the second non-malicious path to cross-tenant data destruction, now routed through guardedUnpin with D-13 race window comment.

Phase 44 scope: TypeScript folder operations that call IPNS publish need caller-side conflict handling (3-way merge with baseChildren param, 4-attempt backoff+jitter, typed ConflictError). Rust parity deferred.

workflow: cleanup-wave helper (worktree.cleanup-wave) must be run from the repo root, not from inside an agent worktree. Running from a worktree subdirectory produces false base_mismatch errors because the helper resolves repoRoot from cwd.

cleanup-wave is not idempotent: re-running it on already-merged entries reports branch_mismatch and aborts the entire run. Workaround: write a reduced manifest containing only the remaining unmerged entries.
Worktree executor agents leave behind node_modules and .husky/_ untracked directories that block the merge step. These must be rm'd before calling cleanup-wave.
zsh multi-glob rm aborts entirely if any glob fails to match: `rm -rf node_modules apps/*/node_modules` fails completely if apps/ has no subdirectories with node_modules. Use single explicit paths.
GSD decision coverage gate uses mechanical grep for literal `D-NN:` citation strings in plan must_haves. If a decision is addressed only implicitly, the gate fails — the citation must be explicit.

Wave executor merge conflicts can leave MERGE_HEAD in the repo. A clean working tree with no conflict markers means all conflicts were auto-resolved; `git commit --no-edit` concludes the merge without re-resolving.

openapi.json accumulates formatting-only drift in the main tree as a side effect of `nest build` during tests. This must be restored with `git checkout --` before merging executor worktrees to avoid spurious conflicts.
When answering user questions during a discussion workflow, answer in plain prose first with code evidence — never re-present option menus without having answered the literal question.

friction: 1Password SSH signing failures mid-session required user to manually restart the desktop app; no automated recovery path exists.
gsd commit helper returns 'committed: false' as a false negative frequently — every commit required a follow-up git log verification, adding overhead and confusion.
cleanup-wave not being idempotent required writing reduced manifest files by hand after partial runs, which is error-prone.
openapi.json formatting drift from nest build side-effects blocked Wave 3 worktree merges until manually restored.
Planner agent died with a socket error after writing 3 of 8 plans, requiring filesystem inspection and a continuation planner agent.
pnpm/jest double-dash bug caused several post-merge test commands to silently run no tests (jest treated the pattern as a positional argument matching nothing).
prettier mangling regex patterns and pipe characters in .planning/ markdown caused a VALIDATION.md test command to break — root cause was no .prettierignore existing.
User had to explicitly call out that the assistant was presenting option menus instead of directly answering their question about endpoint exposure and CID discoverability.
